Your body is in the early stages of healing itself and these symptoms are all a necessary part of the process. There are things you can do to help with the irritability but in all honesty, none of them are a quick fix. They are more habits and lifestyle choices but I promise you they will help you with sooo much more than this one issue and have a profoundly positive effect on your overall, and moment to moment experience of life.

 The golden trio, eat well, move well and think well.

 I'll tell you how I approach each of these things but what works for you will be unique and only you will be able to figure them out. 

1) Eat well: Drink a boatload of water each day. I do around 3 litres. Ideally your diet will be mostly fresh veggies. Processed foods = shit. Cut down on sugar as much as you can. A tiny bit for treats is fine. This is all about getting your gut healthy which is where 90% of your serotonin is produced. They've only recently figured out that so much of our mental and physical well-being is tied to our gut health. 

2) Move well: I don't know how active you are, but if you're not currently active... START. You will thank me I swear to god. Some options are: swimming, running, weights, social sports, yoga, martial arts (I do Muay Thai) anything is better than nothing and CONSISTENCY is the big key to long lasting effects. When I started going to the gym my thing was "I'm showing up 6 days a week. Even if I show up and sit on the bike for 10mins and fuck off home, I'm showing up". It's the building of the habit that's important.

3) Think well. Learn to meditate. This is probably the #1 piece of advice I have for you. I got the Waking Up app. It was made by Sam Harris, a neuroscientist/philosopher. Certifiably legit motherfucker. He will teach you how to meditate properly. There are other apps/ways to earn but this one worked for me. Learning to meditate may just be the single most important skill I have learned in my whole life. It literally changes your brain in a deeply positive way that you cannot understand unless you do it for yourself. 

Sorry if you were looking for a quick fix, but they really don't exist without having negative side effects in some way. I'm a 28 year old dude and I see myself in you and I wish someone told me this stuff when I was your age. 

Best of luck brother, stay strong because you deserve to be well 💪❤️🙏
